key_insight: HVOF-sprayed Ni-20Cr+40TiC reduced oxidation weight gain by 95.71% relative to bare SA516 boiler steel after 50 cycles at 900°C.
engineering_relevance: Ni–Cr-based coatings could improve boiler-steel oxidation resistance through dense protective oxide formation, reduced porosity, and increased microhardness.
method: Apply Ni-20Cr, Ni-20Cr+40TiC, and Ni-20Cr+40TiN coatings using HVOF and plasma spraying.
Characterize microstructure and phases using XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping.
evidence_signal: HVOF Ni-20Cr+40TiC performed best among the tested coatings; coated specimens formed protective oxides, while bare steel showed severe oxide spalling and cracking.
watch_item: Laboratory air-oxidation results do not establish long-term coating durability under corrosive boiler gases or particle erosion.
paper_title: Microstructure and high-temperature oxidation behaviour of HVOF and plasma sprayed Ni–Cr-based ceramic coatings on SA516 boiler steel
